eligibility_reason: Gibson & Levy report two new-data self-paced reading experiments on Mechanical Turk (72 and 72 analyzed participants) that attempt to replicate Hackl, Koster-Hale & Varvoutis (2012) Experiments 1 and 2, a separately published work.

effects.original_title: Quantification and ACD: Evidence from Real Time Sentence Processing
effects.original_authors: Hackl, M.; Koster-Hale, J.; Varvoutis, J.
effects.outcome: Residual self-paced reading times in the words following the ACD relative-clause verb (regions 15-18, critically word 17)
effects.contrast: Interaction of determiner (every vs the) x verb type (ellipsis 'was' vs full verb): 'the'/ellipsis condition especially slow
effects.description: HKV Experiment 1 claimed that ACD (ellipsis) relative clauses modifying an object NP with 'every' are read faster than those modifying an NP with 'the', with no such advantage in full-verb controls, yielding a determiner x verb-type interaction in reading times shortly after the elided verb (supporting quantifier raising).
effects.citation_sentence: In order to better understand the on-line data in HKV's self-paced reading experiments, we therefore attempted to replicate HKV's self-paced reading experiments.
effects.evidence: Section 'Attempted replication of HKV Experiment 1', Results: "But, unlike HKV, we did not find the predicted interaction between verb type and determiner in any of the four regions that we investigated"; Summary: "we have failed to find even hints of the predicted interactions in the locations that HKV found them."
effects.notes: The citation sentence uses the abbreviation HKV, defined earlier as 'Hackl, Koster-Hale & Varvoutis (HKV;2012)'. Original DOI is not stated in the paper (reference gives J. Semantics 29, 145-206), so original_url is left blank; only author initials are given. Interaction was significant by items (F2) at word 18 but not by participants, and later than HKV's effect; authors still frame the result as a failure. The replication also reproduced HKV's main effects of verb type (verb slower at word 15, ellipsis slower at 16-18). These are not coded as separate claims because they are not the finding HKV reported as evidence for QR; a second coder might add them as successes. Replication type: the study ran on Mechanical Turk (online) rather than in the lab, used lightly edited target items (initial NP and verb region only), and used new fillers and comprehension questions. Online administration counts as a context change, hence close extension. Direct is also defensible because the authors meant to reproduce the procedure as closely as they could.

effects.original_title: Quantification and ACD: Evidence from Real Time Sentence Processing
effects.original_authors: Hackl, M.; Koster-Hale, J.; Varvoutis, J.
effects.outcome: Residual self-paced reading times in the words following the ACD relative-clause verb (regions 15-18, critically word 16)
effects.contrast: Interaction of determiner (the vs every) x verb type (full verb / local ellipsis 'did' / long-distance ellipsis 'was'), in the 3x2 design and the restricted 2x2 (full verb vs local ellipsis): 'the'/local-ellipsis especially slow
effects.description: HKV Experiment 2 claimed that 'the' was read more slowly than 'every' only in the local-ellipsis condition, giving a determiner x verb-type interaction (3x2 and 2x2) at the second word after the relative-clause verb, consistent with quantifier raising.
effects.citation_sentence: In order to better understand the on-line data in HKV's self-paced reading experiments, we therefore attempted to replicate HKV's self-paced reading experiments.
effects.evidence: Section 'Attempted replication of HKV Experiment 2', Results: "But, unlike HKV, we did not find the predicted interaction between verb type and determiner in the full 3x2 design ... Nor did we find the predicted interaction between verb type and determiner in the restricted 2x2 conditions"; mixed-effects models "showed no reliable interactions in any word position."
effects.notes: The 3x2 and 2x2 interaction tests check the same claim, so they are coded as one entry. A marginal interaction at word 16 went in the direction opposite to the QR prediction, but it was not significant (p=.12/.066 for the 2x2), so this is not a reversal. The main effect of verb type at words 16-17 (long-distance ellipsis slower) was replicated but is not coded as a separate claim (see the Exp 1 notes). The target items were HKV's originals. Fillers and comprehension questions were new, and the study ran on MTurk (online), hence close extension; direct is also defensible. Original DOI is not stated in the paper.
